methodologyNotes: Roster covers 13 cellular and non-cellular trail / game cameras. Every product re-verified 2026-06-19 against the manufacturer page plus a specialist reviewer (primarily trailcampro.com) and/or a major retailer. trigger_speed_sec is the picture-mode trigger in seconds (specialist-measured where available, else manufacturer-rated); detection_range_ft is the manufacturer-RATED PIR detection distance in feet (kept consistent across the roster rather than mixing measured and rated values); flash_type uses no_glow / low_glow / white, with red-glow / 850 nm IR mapped to low_glow per the three-value vocabulary; cellular is a boolean (true = built-in LTE radio); megapixels are the native sensor value where disclosed, else null (most models advertise interpolated MP only); priceUsd is the US MSRP or a published retail price as a number; null denotes a genuinely unverified value. Corrections this pass: spypoint-force-pro price 99.99->169.95 (the $99.99 figure was unsupported; TrailCamPro regular price is $169.95 and Spypoint MSRP is well above $99.99); bushnell-cellucore-30 trigger 0.2->0.35, detection 100->80, flash no_glow->low_glow (TrailCamPro measures 0.35 s, 80 ft, red-glow IR); stealth-cam-fusion-x-pro detection 70->80 (rated value, for methodology consistency). accessedAt 2026-06-19.

TrailCamPro measured 0.36 s trigger and classifies the flash as red-glow (mapped to low_glow). Native megapixels not disclosed (4K via interpolation), so megapixels=null.

products.name: Browning Recon Force Elite HP5
products.priceNote: TrailCamPro lists "Sale price $179.95" for the Browning Recon Force Elite HP5 (Non-Cellular), sold out at time of access; used as the US retail price.
products.provenance: TrailCamPro's product page (titled "Browning Recon Force Elite HP5 (Non-Cellular)", Model #BTC-7E-HP5, "the 2022 Recon Force Elite HP5") confirms the exact model — not the current 46 MP/1440p HP5 Ultra sibling nor the no-glow Spec Ops HP5 — and lists 24 mpxl (interpolated) photos, 1920x1080 (1080p) MP4 video, Red Glow IR (mapped to low_glow), 8 AA batteries, and the "$179.95" sale price used as the US retail figure. NatureSpy's dated Nov 25 2022 deep-dive corroborates the 2022 Recon Force Elite HP5 low-glow variant: up-to-24 MP interpolated photos, 1920x1080 full HD video, low-glow LEDs with a dim red glow, "Long (100ft)" detection, "Fast (0.1s)" trigger, 8x lithium AA, and 2022 release. detection_range_ft uses the manufacturer-rated 100 ft (per roster methodology; TrailCamPro's measured value is 80 ft); trigger_speed_sec uses the verbatim manufacturer-rated 0.1 s (TrailCamPro's page shows an implausible 0.02 s picture trigger, treated as a transcription artifact). The Browning manufacturer product page now redirects to its homepage (this 2022 model is discontinued), so TrailCamPro is used as source.url, consistent with the roster's existing Browning/Reconyx/Bushnell entries.
